For 'carry the key on at least two different moves' only two steps are needed; the machine overcounts by one and can never reach u3 in two moves. Reachability also fails: key_lost self-loops/fall-backs are fine, but if key_lost fires at u1/u2 the RM returns to u0 and requires re-earning steps that already occurred (has_key&!key_lost events are one-step conditions, so the same two carried moves cannot be re-used after recovery—agent must pick up and carry again, which arguably still satisfies the task but makes progress rewards misaligned). More critically, u3 (accepting/final) is never reachable via a two-move carry: from u0, move 1 -> u1, move 2 -> u2, and the episode can end with the agent never reaching FINAL_STATES, so the task is not recognized. Compactness: states u2 is superfluous if u2->u3 should not exist; restructure so u2 is final after two carried moves. Also, the FINAL_STATES header is present but the accepting state itself only rewards 1.0 on a transition that requires three moves; final/accepting state semantics appear inverted. Fix: make reaching the second has_key-carry step the final state and give the terminal reward there.
